description: Random init; prints the task object's public attributes to learn vocab and sequence format.

1 block, 1 head, no LayerNorm: attention reads the place-value partial sum S_p for each output place (higher digits masked, '+' absorbs spare mass); MLP wraps at 10; linear head is a parabolic digit classifier. NOTE: 200/200 on eval but fails 106/51285 adversarial near-carry inputs (top-digit float32/gap bug), fixed in v2.
Same circuit as v1 with the gap corrected to 1e-5 (top place) and float64 weights, to fix top-digit failures on near-carry inputs found by the adversarial self-test.
Attention-only long division, no MLP or LayerNorm: head A adds (a+b)/10^p, head B subtracts the printed digits (restricted by the causal mask), head classifies the remainder in [0,10).
Long division with rank-2 attention scores ln(10)*(q-p) and a 1e18 constant sink on '+', so d_model drops from 22 to 8 and position embeddings hold place values instead of one-hot codes.
Low-rank long division with the attention output projection W_o removed: each head writes to a reserved residual slot and the output head subtracts them.
Long division with rectangular attention (2-dim queries/keys, 1-dim values), a 1-dim token embedding, a 5-dim position embedding and a 3-input head, removing every weight the circuit never uses.
Negative control: long_division_rect in float32, to measure how much the design relies on float64 precision. Self-test 64101/129285.

Float32 carry-lookahead: one head reads the lower-place sum, one reads the integer digit pair; MLP ramps make crisp CARRY and WRAP bits, and a parabolic head classifies the integer P + CARRY - 10 WRAP.

Six blocks forming a ripple-carry chain, one full adder per place: attention fetches the digit pair, the MLP computes the carry and writes the digit only at the position printing that place. All signals are small integers.

One weight-tied full-adder block applied six times, like a recurrent cell: a STEP register queries the digit pair and a TTL countdown register triggers printing, both shifted by the MLP. NOTE: the snapshot docstring's 'all margins at least 0.5' holds for signal rounding only; ripple_shared_noise1pct shows it does not hold for weight noise.
Robustness test: ripple_shared_cell run entirely in float16, compared with long_division_rect which fails even in float32. Self-test 129285/129285.
Robustness test: ripple_shared_cell with 1% seeded multiplicative Gaussian noise on every weight, measuring the circuit's tolerance to weight perturbation. Self-test 46/129285.
Digital ripple-carry cell: one-hot digits, one head per operand, and an MLP that is the literal full-adder truth table of restoring AND gates, applied six times with shared weights.

Robustness test: truth_table_adder with 1% seeded multiplicative Gaussian noise on every weight, the same condition that broke the analog ripple cell. NOTE: 200/200 on eval but self-test only 119852/129285; carries decayed along propagate chains.

Truth-table adder with saturating carry gates (clamped ramps from two ReLUs) under 1% weight noise, so a weakened carry is restored at each place instead of decaying along a propagate chain. Self-test 129285/129285 on noise seed 0 only.
Breaking-point search: saturating truth-table adder under 5% seeded multiplicative weight noise. Self-test 37331/129285.

Truth-table adder with STEP and TTL bits also passed through clamped ramps on every shift, under 5% weight noise, testing whether register decay caused the failures at high places. Hypothesis not supported: self-test 37857/129285, barely changed.
Breaking-point search: truth-table adder with restored registers under 2% seeded multiplicative weight noise. Self-test 91735/129285.

The crisp carry circuit in the unmodified default architecture (64 dims, 4 heads, 3 layers, LayerNorm): mirrored signals and a +/-B ballast pair turn LayerNorm into a constant rescale; blocks 1-2 are zero. Fails in float32: self-test 24565/129285.
crisp_carry_original_arch in float64, testing whether float32 rounding of the +/-B ballast in LayerNorm's mean caused the lost carries. Hypothesis supported: self-test 129285/129285.
Smallest long division: W_q, W_k and W_v replaced by fixed wiring, leaving only a 1-dim token embedding, a 4-dim position embedding and a 3-input head.
Sink-mass sweep: long_division_fixed_wiring with C = 1e16, predicted to pass since the normaliser error stays below the 5e-6 classifier margin.

Sink-mass sweep: long_division_fixed_wiring with C = 1e14, predicted to fail because the normaliser error exceeds the 5e-6 classifier margin. Prediction was wrong: self-test 129285/129285, because the error is one-sided and upward.

Sink-mass sweep: C = 1e10, below the corrected failure estimate of 1.6e10, where the one-sided positive bias in R should reach a full unit at place 0. Prediction confirmed: self-test 109732/129285 with last-digit +1 errors.
Robustness control: long_division_minimal with 1e-6 seeded multiplicative weight noise, to compare with the one-hot adder's 1% tolerance. Self-test 43467/129285.
Robustness control: long_division_minimal with 1e-9 seeded multiplicative weight noise, bracketing the tolerance of the precise analog design. Self-test 129285/129285.
Seed check: truth-table adder with restored registers under 1% weight noise with noise seed 1, testing whether the seed-0 pass was luck. NOTE: 200/200 on eval but self-test 129186/129285.
Seed check: truth-table adder with restored registers under 1% weight noise with noise seed 2, the second repeat of the seed-0 result. Self-test 127076/129285.
Smallest verified circuit: fixed-wiring long division with sink mass 1e12, about 60x above its measured failure point, and a head reading only (1, R); 108 parameters, float64.
